beats.text: About 300 people were lost in one night on Lake Michigan.
beats.label: LAKE MICHIGAN, 1860
beats.credit: Wisconsin Historical Society; Encyclopedia of Milwaukee

beats.text: September 8, 1860. The steamer Lady Elgin was carrying an estimated 400 people home from Chicago to Milwaukee. Most were Irish residents of Milwaukee's Third Ward.
beats.label: SEPTEMBER 8, 1860
beats.credit: Encyclopedia of Milwaukee; Milwaukee County Historical Society

beats.text: Around 2:30 in the morning, in high winds and heavy rain, the schooner Augusta struck her.
beats.label: 2:30 IN THE MORNING
beats.credit: Wisconsin Historical Society; Encyclopedia of Milwaukee

beats.text: The Lady Elgin broke up and sank in less than half an hour, miles off Winnetka, Illinois.
beats.label: OFF WINNETKA, ILLINOIS
beats.credit: History of the Great Lakes (1899); Brendon Baillod

beats.text: On shore, a Northwestern student named Edward Spencer pulled people from the surf. He is credited with saving 17.
beats.label: EDWARD SPENCER

beats.text: Her captain was among the lost. Milwaukee's Third Ward was devastated.
beats.label: MILWAUKEE'S THIRD WARD
beats.credit: Encyclopedia of Milwaukee; History of the Great Lakes (1899)

beats.text: The wreck was found in 1989, off Highland Park, Illinois.
beats.label: FOUND IN 1989
